data.summary: Execute a child tool synchronously or park until an asynchronous child result resumes the parent.

requiredFields.note: Published version of the tool to run, a non-empty string. Publishing never moves it: a newer version runs only once this value names it. Missing, the node fails, no edge.

optionalFields.note: A string or a non-negative integer. The engine never reads it on this node.
Values handed to the tool, keyed by the tool's input name. Absent means {}. Each value is a template string or { type?, value }.
One input: a template string, read as STRING, or { type?, value }, closed, both strings (no type reads as STRING). Interpolated before the tool starts; it reaches the tool under this key.
How value is read: 'BOOLEAN', 'NUMBER', 'OBJECT' or 'ARRAY' are interpolated then JSON-parsed; any other string ('STRING', 'ENUM'...) stays an interpolated string. Use the input's type.
The value, always a string template ({{$memory.x}}). With a JSON type write '42', 'true' or '[1,2]'. If it does not parse, the tool gets the raw text, not interpolated.
Memory key that gets the value of the output the tool ends on; absent means 'response'. Synchronous: stored before routing, when truthy. Async: stored on resume, only if an edge matches.
Optional DLP settings. With isDlpEnabled and at least one rule, the logged inputs and the output value are scrubbed, in debug and normal runs. The tool receives the inputs unscrubbed.
Absent or true parks this workflow while the tool runs and resumes it when the tool ends; false waits inline. Forced false when an AI_TASK agent started the run. Async follows one edge only.
true holds the user while an async call is parked: their messages get blockedMessage instead of reaching the flow, for up to 300 s by default. Default false. Ignored when synchronous.
Reply to a user who writes while isBlockingEnabled holds them; a template, resolved when the node parks. Empty or absent: their messages are dropped without a reply.
Display label per input key. No effect on execution: the engine reads input.
One label.
Deprecated copy of the tool version's outputs: [{ id, name, displayName?, type }]. No effect on execution.
One output.
Output id.
Output name.
Optional display name.
Output type, a string.
Id of the tool to call: a non-blank string or a positive integer. The engine reads it before toolData.toolId.
Tool reference: { toolId, toolkitId? } plus a copy of the tool's own settings (toolName, workflowId, thumbnail, colors), closed. Required unless the top-level toolId is set.
Id of the tool: a non-blank string or a positive integer. Read only when the top-level toolId is absent.
A string or a non-negative integer. The engine never reads it on this node.
Id of the tool's own workflow, a non-negative integer. No effect on execution: the engine runs the tool by toolId and version.

outletDocs.description: The tool ended on an output that is not FAILED: only the edges whose handle carries that output's id continue, after its value is stored under variable.
outletDocs.fires: Synchronous: every matching edge fans out in stored order. Async: on resume, the first matching edge only. None matching ends the flow there. A plain success edge never fires.

branches.description: Continue here when the tool ends on this output.
branches.when: One edge per output you handle; none is required. <output-id> is the id of one of the tool's outputs, never its name or the tool's: any other text never fires, silently.

outletDocs.description: The tool ended on a FAILED output: only the edges whose handle carries that output's id continue, after its value is stored under variable (async: only if an edge matches).
outletDocs.fires: Output type FAILED. None matching: the error handler answers, if set. No output (timeout, 30 s by default; depth cap; missing id or version; failed dispatch) follows no edge at all.

branches.description: Continue here when the tool ends on this FAILED output.
branches.when: Output ids are frozen per published version: use one the pinned version declares. A plain success or failed edge never fires.

outletDocs.description: An async call started: this workflow parks on the node and continues when the tool ends, through result_id or error, on the edge carrying that output's id.
outletDocs.fires: async is not false, the run is not synchronous by origin, and the dispatch returns an execution id. Not connectable: no branch token writes it.

notes: Internal tools ONLY — marketplace apps (payments, jelou-kyc) are MCP nodes, not TOOL.
Real toolId/workflowId/thumbnail/version and the output ids come from `jelou tool show <slug|id>` and `jelou tool versions <slug>`; the validator does not check server existence.
Title is server-owned (canvas renders toolData.toolName); custom titles are ignored on push.

Tools may call tools. Depth is capped at TOOL_MAX_NESTING_DEPTH (default 5) — exceeding it fails the node with NESTING_DEPTH_EXCEEDED; a toolId that re-enters its own call chain also logs a TOOL_RECURSION_DETECTED warning. The workflows server rejects on save only the direct self-reference.
Route by the stable child output ID after stripping only the evidenced legacy handle prefixes; never use an output index.
Async dispatch parks only after receiving a child execution ID and resumes through the service-owned callback path.
A missing dynamic result connection preserves the legacy response-path behavior and does not invent an implicit destination.
Route by a stable child output ID after stripping only the three engine prefixes; preserve candidate order and multiplicity.
Precondition: The tool, version, input mapping, permissions, and execution mode are resolved by authorized services.

rules: Never write a START node. The tool adds the workflow's one START (`validate --fix` and `jelou push` write it), unless the workflow enters only through a WEBHOOK.
Your first edge is { "sourceId": "START", "targetId": "<first-node>", "branch": "default" }. "START" is a reserved alias the tool resolves to the real START id; no other node may use that id.
The first node cannot be START, WEBHOOK, EMPTY, NOTE.
WEBHOOK is optional, at most one per workflow, and never chained to START.

A workflow or tool that enters only through a WEBHOOK needs no START: write no edge from "START" and the tool adds none. A channel message or a TOOL node never starts it then. A marketplace skill always needs START.
Next to a wired WEBHOOK that feeds the flow, a START with no edge is only a warning: the tool wires nothing to it and push keeps it.
